verdicts.summary: Waiter timeout does not kill the shared fetch; the fetch runs in the service scope with its own bound.
verdicts.scenario: Status poll times out at 5s, or its caller is interrupted, while the fetch is hung. I checked whether that interrupts or leaks the fetch.

verdicts.summary: The unbounded Fiber.await in pull is the same hazard as finding 0.
verdicts.scenario: Pull waits on a slow status fetch before its 30s timeout starts. The retry path I read is guarded by HEAD, branch and a single merge ref, so it adds no separate hazard.

verdicts.summary: forceKillAfterMs reaches the spawner as a millisecond number, and the spawner accepts it as a Duration.
verdicts.scenario: Callers that do not set the option pass undefined; the spawner then takes the old grace-only path and never sends SIGKILL, as before. The fetch passes 1000 and gets SIGKILL after 1s.
